question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: The rider who met with a accident was not wearing a helmet, the police said.
option_2: The rider who met with an accident was not wearing an helmet, the police said.
option_3: A rider who met with the accident was not wearing the helmet, an police said.
option_4: The rider who met with the accident was not wearing a helmet, the police said.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The rider who met with the accident was not wearing a helmet, the police said.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule — Article "a" vs "an": The article "a" is used before words beginning with a consonant sound, and "an" is used before words beginning with a vowel sound. The word "accident" begins with the vowel sound /æ/, so it takes "an accident"; the word "helmet" begins with the consonant sound /h/, so it takes "a helmet".

• In Option 4, the phrase "met with the accident" uses the definite article "the", which is correct here because the accident being referred to is a specific, particular incident already known to the speaker (the police officer reporting it) — the definite article is used for a specific person, place or thing already identified in the context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "met with a accident" wrongly uses "a" before the vowel sound "accident"; it should be "an accident".

• Option 2 is incorrect because "not wearing an helmet" wrongly uses "an" before the consonant sound "helmet"; it should be "a helmet".

• Option 3 is incorrect because "an police said" wrongly uses "an" before the consonant sound "police"; it should be "the police said" (or "a policeman said").

NOTE

• The choice of article depends on the sound, not the spelling, of the following word — e.g., "an hour" (silent h) but "a university" (sounds like "yoo-").

• Common SSC trap words: hour, honest, heir (take "an"); European, university, one-eyed, useful (take "a") despite starting with a vowel letter.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Gift of the gab
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Fluency of speech.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Gift of the gab" means the natural talent or ability to speak fluently, confidently and persuasively. (धाराप्रवाह बोलने की क्षमता)
◦ Example: The salesman had such a gift of the gab that he convinced everyone to buy the product.

• The word "gab" is an informal term for talk or chatter, and having a "gift" of it means one is naturally skilled at talking.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Freedom of speech (अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता): The right to express one's opinions without restraint — an unrelated legal/political concept.

• Option 3: First speech: Has no idiomatic meaning; it is simply a literal phrase.

• Option 4: Figures of speech (अलंकार): Refers to expressions like similes, metaphors, etc., used to create special effect — not related to fluency.

NOTE

• Other idioms about speaking ability often asked in SSC: "To talk nineteen to the dozen" (to talk very fast), "To speak one's mind" (to say exactly what one thinks), and "Tongue-tied" (unable to speak due to nervousness).

question:
Select the correct homonym to fill in the blank in the given sentence.
I will just ________ some figures for comparison.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. cite.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "cite" means to mention or refer to something as an example or evidence, especially in support of an argument. (उदाहरण या प्रमाण के रूप में उल्लेख करना)
◦ Example: I will just cite some figures for comparison.

• In the given sentence, the speaker is going to refer to/quote some figures for the purpose of comparison, so "cite" is the appropriate word.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "cete" is not a standard English word used in this context (a "cete" is an obscure collective noun for a group of badgers) and does not fit the sentence.

• Option 3: "site" means a location or a place (e.g., a construction site, a website); it does not mean "to refer to".

• Option 4: "sight" means the ability to see, or something seen (a view); it also does not fit the meaning required here.

NOTE

• Cite, site and sight are commonly confused homonyms in SSC exams: cite (to quote/refer), site (a place/location), sight (vision/a view).

• Other frequently tested homonym sets: "here/hear", "there/their/they're", "principal/principle", "stationary/stationery".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

"Do you want to join us for lunch?" / "I'm sorry / my physics class will start at 1 p.m. / and doesn't finish till 3 p.m.""
option_1: my physics class will start at 1 p.m.
option_4: Do you want to join us for lunch?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. my physics class will start at 1 p.m.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule — Simple Present Tense for fixed schedules/timetables: When talking about a fixed, scheduled or timetabled event (classes, trains, flights, shows, etc.), the Simple Present Tense is used instead of the future tense with "will", even though the event is technically in the future.
◦ Example: The train leaves at 6 p.m. (NOT "will leave")

• In the given sentence, the speaker is referring to a fixed class timing (a timetabled event), so the correct form is "my physics class starts at 1 p.m.", not "my physics class will start at 1 p.m."

• This also keeps the sentence consistent with the second clause, "and doesn't finish till 3 p.m.", which is correctly in the Simple Present Tense — both clauses describing the same fixed schedule must use the same tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "I'm sorry" is grammatically correct — a standard polite expression of apology/regret.

• Option 3: "and doesn't finish till 3 p.m." is correct — it rightly uses the Simple Present Tense for the fixed schedule.

• Option 4: "Do you want to join us for lunch?" is a correctly formed interrogative sentence in the Simple Present Tense.

NOTE

• The Simple Present Tense is also used for: (i) universal truths (The sun rises in the east), (ii) habitual actions (He goes for a walk every morning), and (iii) fixed timetabled/scheduled future events, as tested in this question.

• Words like "till/until", "before", "after", "as soon as" in a time clause referring to the future are also usually followed by the Simple Present, not "will".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Tedious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Tiresome.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Tedious" means causing weariness or boredom because it is too long, slow or dull. (उबाऊ, थकाऊ)
◦ Example: Filling out the lengthy government form was a tedious task.

• "Tiresome" carries the same sense of being wearisome and boring, making it the closest synonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Wholesome" (स्वस्थकर): Means healthy or beneficial to physical, mental or moral well-being — the opposite sense of "tedious".

• Option 3: "Repetitive" (दोहराव वाला): Means done or occurring repeatedly; a tedious task is often repetitive, but the words are not synonymous — repetition is only one possible cause of tedium, not its meaning.

• Option 4: "Threescore" (साठ): An archaic word simply meaning "sixty"; unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "tedious" useful for SSC: monotonous, wearisome, dreary, humdrum, laborious.

• Antonym to remember: "tedious" ↔ "interesting/exciting".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
He just needs to calm down a wee bit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. agitate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "calm down" means to become quiet or less angry/excited, or to make someone do so. (शांत होना)

• "Agitate" means to make someone troubled, excited or anxious, which is the direct opposite of becoming calm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "understand" (समझना): Means to grasp the meaning of something; not related in meaning to "calm down" or its opposite.

• Option 3: "question" (प्रश्न करना): Means to ask or express doubt about something; unrelated to the emotional state of calmness.

• Option 4: "dissipate" (छितराना): Means to disperse or scatter, or to disappear gradually; it is not an antonym of "calm down" — in fact, when anger "dissipates", a person becomes calmer, so this is closer to a synonym in sense, not an opposite.

NOTE

• Other antonym pairs of "calm" often tested in SSC: calm ↔ agitated/turbulent/frantic/upset.

• Related idiom: "To calm down" vs "To fly off the handle" (to suddenly become very angry).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
The benevolent gesture of the rich merchant was appreciated by all.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Generous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Benevolent" means well-meaning, kind and generous, especially in giving help or money to those in need. (दयालु, उदार)
◦ Example: The benevolent merchant donated a large sum to the flood victims.

• "Generous" carries the same sense of being kind and willing to give, making it the closest synonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Sombre" (उदास, गंभीर): Means dark, dull or gloomy in mood or colour; unrelated to kindness.

• Option 3: "Numb" (सुन्न): Means unable to feel or move normally, physically or emotionally; unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4: "Sober" (गंभीर, शांत): Means serious, moderate, or not affected by alcohol; unrelated to generosity.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "benevolent": charitable, kind-hearted, philanthropic, magnanimous.

• Antonym to remember: "benevolent" ↔ "malevolent" (wishing harm to others).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.
He is very ___________ (Eager) to join the Air Force.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. keen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Eager" means having or showing keen interest, enthusiasm, or desire. (उत्सुक)
◦ Example: He is very keen to join the Air Force.

• "Keen" carries the same sense of strong enthusiasm or desire, making it the closest synonym of "eager" in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "irksome" (कष्टप्रद): Means annoying or tiresome; it has a negative sense, opposite to enthusiasm.

• Option 3: "dubious" (संदिग्ध): Means doubtful or of questionable value; unrelated to eagerness.

• Option 4: "unconcerned" (उदासीन): Means not interested or worried; this is nearly the opposite of "eager".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "eager": enthusiastic, avid, ardent, zealous.

• Antonym to remember: "eager" ↔ "reluctant/indifferent".

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The company is launching a new product next month.
option_1: The new product will be launched by the company next month.
option_2: A new product is being launched by the company next month.
option_3: The launching of a new product by the company is next month.
option_4: Next month, the company will launch a new product.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A new product is being launched by the company next month.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The company is launching a new product next month" is in the Present Continuous Tense (used here for a planned future action).

• Rule — Present Continuous Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + is/am/are + V-ing + Object
◦ Passive: Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "a new product" becomes the subject "a new product"; the auxiliary "is being" is used (singular subject); the verb "launching" becomes the past participle "launched"; and "the company" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: A new product is being launched by the company next month.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "will be launched" is the passive of the Simple Future Tense, not the Present Continuous Tense of the original sentence.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "The launching of a new product by the company is next month" changes the sentence structure awkwardly and does not follow the standard passive voice construction.

• Option 4 is incorrect because it is not in passive voice at all — it merely reorders the active sentence, keeping "the company" as the subject and "will launch" as an active verb.

NOTE

• Present Continuous is often used, as in this question, to describe planned/fixed future arrangements (e.g., "We are meeting him tomorrow").

• Passive voice is generally not formed for intransitive verbs (verbs without an object), and modal/continuous forms must retain their same tense/aspect when converted to passive.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Get into a scrape
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Involved in a problem.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Get into a scrape" means to get involved in an awkward, difficult or troublesome situation. (मुसीबत में पड़ना)
◦ Example: He often gets into a scrape by not thinking before he acts.

• The word "scrape" here is used informally to mean "a difficult or embarrassing predicament", so to "get into" one means to become caught up in such a situation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Creating a problem": Suggests actively causing trouble for someone else, which is not what the idiom conveys — the idiom is about being caught in trouble oneself.

• Option 2: "Solving a problem": Means the opposite — resolving a difficulty, not getting into one.

• Option 3: "Explaining a problem": Means describing or clarifying an issue, unrelated to the idiom's meaning.

NOTE

• Other idioms using "trouble/difficulty" often asked in SSC: "To be in hot water" (to be in trouble), "To be in a fix" (to be in a difficult situation), and "To get out of a scrape" (to escape from a difficult situation).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Person who betrays his own country.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Traitor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Traitor" is a person who betrays their own country, a cause, or someone's trust, especially by helping an enemy. (देशद्रोही)
◦ Example: The traitor was arrested for leaking military secrets to the enemy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Mascot" (शुभंकर): A person, animal or object adopted as a symbol of good luck for a group or event; unrelated to betrayal.

• Option 3: "Icon" (प्रतीक/आदर्श): A famous person or thing regarded as a representative symbol of something; carries a positive sense, opposite to "traitor".

• Option 4: "Paragon" (आदर्श व्यक्ति): A person who is a perfect example of a particular quality, i.e., a model of excellence; also positive, unrelated to betrayal.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions often tested in SSC: "Turncoat" (a person who changes their principles/allegiance), "Renegade" (a person who deserts a cause), and "Patriot" (a person who loves and loyally supports their country — the opposite of "traitor").

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Devide.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Divide" — to separate something into parts, or to perform the mathematical operation of division.

• Spelling key: The word begins with "Di-" (meaning "apart/in two"), not "De-". Compare with other "Di-" words like "Divert", "Direct".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Provide" is correctly spelt — meaning to make something available for use.

• Option 3: "Subside" is correctly spelt — meaning to become less intense or to settle down.

• Option 4: "Confide" is correctly spelt — meaning to tell someone a secret or private matter in trust.

NOTE

• Common SSC misspelling trap: "Divide" is often wrongly written as "Devide" by confusing the prefixes "Di-" and "De-".

• Other frequently confused prefix pairs in SSC spelling questions: "Dessert/Desert", "Decent/Descent", "Precede/Proceed".

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. But at the same time, this is also true that when one reads a few works of the same genre, one naturally comes to know a rough structure of that genre.
B. The essence of suspense is whether the reader will be able to gauge the criminal before the detective tells who he is.
C. This leads to a different kind of approach to understanding literature in general and detective fiction in particular.
D. It is found that when one knows a genre and its structure and rules, it may often not make us enjoy a piece of literary work in the same manner as one usually does.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. DACB.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence D is the best opening sentence — it introduces the general finding/premise: knowing a genre and its rules may reduce one's enjoyment of a literary work.

• Sentence A logically follows D with the contrasting conjunction "But at the same time", adding that reading works of a genre also naturally teaches its structure — linking directly back to the idea of "knowing a genre" in D.

• Sentence C follows A with "This leads to...", where "This" refers back to the point made in A, drawing a conclusion about a different approach to understanding literature in general and detective fiction in particular.

• Sentence B logically comes last, narrowing the general idea of "detective fiction" (introduced at the end of C) down to the specific essence of suspense in detective fiction.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. DACB.

Additional Information

• Option 2 (BDCA): Incorrect because starting with B (about suspense specifically) before the general premise about genre and structure (D) breaks the logical flow from general to specific.

• Option 3 (CBAD): Incorrect because C uses "This leads to...", which requires an antecedent idea before it; starting the paragraph with C leaves "This" without any reference.

• Option 4 (ADCB): Incorrect because A starts with "But at the same time", a contrasting connector that requires a preceding idea to contrast with; it cannot be the opening sentence.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, look for linking words/pronouns such as "But", "This", "However", "Therefore" — these words point to an idea that must have already been introduced in a previous sentence, helping fix the correct sequence.

• A sentence containing a general statement/premise usually comes before sentences that elaborate, contrast, or narrow it down to specifics.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
In today's digital age, information is widely available to everyone by many means of media such as television, newspapers, films, and social media.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. via various forms.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined segment "by many means" needs to be replaced by an expression that fits naturally with "of media such as television, newspapers, films, and social media" — i.e., it must correctly collocate with "media" and preserve the original meaning ("through many different types/forms").

• "Via various forms" correctly conveys "through various forms" and grammatically fits with "of media" that follows — "via various forms of media" is a natural and idiomatic English expression.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "with quite enough of mechanisms" is incorrect — "mechanisms of media" is not idiomatic, and "quite enough" changes the meaning to sufficiency rather than variety.

• Option 2: "through any strategies" is incorrect — "strategies of media" is not a natural collocation, and "strategies" refers to plans of action, not channels/types of media.

• Option 4: "among many techniques" is incorrect — "techniques of media" is not idiomatic; "techniques" refers to methods/skills, not different types of media.

NOTE

• When replacing an underlined segment, always check that the replacement fits grammatically and idiomatically with the words immediately before and after it in the sentence — here, the deciding factor is the natural collocation "forms of media".

• Words like "means", "forms", "modes", "channels" are commonly used interchangeably to refer to types of media/communication in SSC sentence-improvement questions.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Solusion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Solution" — an answer to a problem, or a liquid mixture in chemistry.

• Spelling key: The ending is "-tion" (as in most nouns formed from verbs like "solve" → "solution"), not "-sion". Compare with other "-tion" words: "Question", "Attention", "Caution".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Bonafide" is correctly spelt — meaning genuine or real (from Latin, "in good faith").

• Option 2: "Cultural" is correctly spelt — relating to the culture of a particular society.

• Option 4: "Trustworthy" is correctly spelt — meaning able to be relied on as honest or truthful.

NOTE

• Common SSC misspelling trap: words ending in the sound "-shun" are sometimes wrongly spelt with "-sion" instead of the correct "-tion", or vice versa.

• Rule of thumb: nouns derived from verbs ending in "-de", "-se", "-ss", "-mit" usually take "-sion" (e.g., decide→decision, permit→permission), while most others take "-tion" (e.g., solve→solution, act→action).

question: Describe how you will tell your friends that someone has picked Suman's pocket in passive voice.
option_1: Someone has being picked Suman's pocket.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Suman's pocket has been picked.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Someone has picked Suman's pocket" is in the Present Perfect Tense.

• Rule — Present Perfect Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + has/have + been + V3 + (+ by + Subject, if needed)

• Applying the rule: the object "Suman's pocket" becomes the subject; the auxiliary "has been" is used (singular subject); and the verb "picked" (already V3, since "pick" is a regular verb) is retained. The agent "someone" is dropped, as is common when the doer is unknown or unimportant.
◦ Passive: Suman's pocket has been picked.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "has being picked" wrongly uses "being" instead of "been"; the correct passive auxiliary for Present Perfect is "has/have + been + V3", not "has + being".

• Option 2 is incorrect because "had picked" is an active-voice, Past Perfect Tense form, not a passive construction at all.

• Option 3 is incorrect because it drops the auxiliary "has" — the correct passive form requires "has been picked", not just "been picked".

NOTE

• A very common SSC error is confusing "being" (used in continuous-tense passives, e.g., "is being done") with "been" (used in perfect-tense passives, e.g., "has been done").

• When the doer of the action is unknown, unimportant, or obvious from context (as with "someone"), the "by + agent" phrase is often omitted in the passive sentence.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
'Habitual' may be replaced by '_________'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Continual.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Habitual" means done constantly or as a habit; usual or customary. (आदतन, नियमित)
◦ Example: His habitual lateness annoyed his colleagues.

• "Continual" means happening frequently or repeatedly over a period of time, which closely matches the sense of something occurring again and again as a habit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Stagnant" (स्थिर, ठहरा हुआ): Means not moving, flowing, or developing; changing very little — unrelated to "habitual".

• Option 3: "Temperate" (समशीतोष्ण, संयमित): Means showing moderation or self-restraint, or (of climate) mild; unrelated to "habitual".

• Option 4: "Holistic" (समग्र): Means dealing with or treating the whole of something, not just a part; unrelated to "habitual".

NOTE

• Distinguish "continual" (frequently repeated, often with breaks) from "continuous" (happening without any interruption) — both relate to repetition/persistence but are subtly different.

• Other synonyms of "habitual": customary, regular, chronic, routine.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The match schedule was disturbed due to _________ rains.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. incessant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Incessant" means continuing without pause or interruption. (लगातार, अविराम)
◦ Example: The match schedule was disturbed due to incessant rains.

• Rains that continue without stopping are the most logical reason for a match schedule being disturbed, making "incessant" the appropriate word.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "detestable" (घृणित): Means deserving intense dislike; does not describe rain in a meaningful, collocating way.

• Option 3: "venerable" (सम्माननीय): Means accorded great respect, typically because of age, wisdom or character; used for people/institutions, not rain.

• Option 4: "soothing" (सुखदायक): Means having a calming or comforting effect; the opposite of something that would disturb a match schedule.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "incessant": continuous, ceaseless, unrelenting, persistent, non-stop.

• Common SSC collocations: "incessant rain/noise/chatter", "torrential rain", "heavy downpour".

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. It could possibly lead to serious injuries, hence a mate for N' Pongo became inevitable.
B. Within the span of one year, N' Pongo grew double the size and the need to obtain a mate for him arose, for it becomes unsafe for the humans around.
C. Every afternoon he was brought out onto the lawn to show off his skills in front of his admirers.
D. Owing to his attractive appearance and disposition, good manners and a well-developed sense of humor, N' Pongo soon became the darling of the zoo.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. DCBA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence D is the best opening sentence — it introduces the subject, N' Pongo, and explains how he became "the darling of the zoo" because of his appearance and manners, setting up the context for the paragraph.

• Sentence C logically follows D by elaborating on how N' Pongo displayed his "attractive appearance and disposition" — being shown off every afternoon in front of his admirers.

• Sentence B follows next, introducing a shift/problem: over time, N' Pongo grew bigger and became unsafe for the humans around him, creating the need for a mate.

• Sentence A logically concludes the paragraph, following directly from B with "It could possibly lead to serious injuries", explaining the consequence of the danger mentioned in B and confirming that a mate for N' Pongo became inevitable.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. DCBA.

Additional Information

• Option 2 (DABC): Incorrect because placing A (about "serious injuries" and a mate becoming "inevitable") right after D breaks the logical flow — the danger described in A is a consequence of B, which has not yet been introduced.

• Option 3 (CDAB): Incorrect because starting with C (using the pronoun "he" for N' Pongo) before D (which introduces N' Pongo by name) leaves "he" without a clear antecedent.

• Option 4 (BDAC): Incorrect because starting with B skips the introductory context in D, and disrupts the cause-effect link between B (the danger) and A (its consequence).

NOTE

• In para-jumbles involving a named subject (here, "N' Pongo"), the sentence that first introduces the subject by name usually comes before sentences that refer to them only with a pronoun like "he"/"him".

• Look for cause-and-effect pairs — here, B (the cause: growing size/danger) must be immediately followed by A (the effect: risk of injury and a mate becoming inevitable).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
The study of evolution of mankind
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Anthropology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Anthropology" means the study of human beings, their origin, evolution, physical characteristics, and social customs. (मानव विज्ञान)
◦ Example: She studied anthropology to understand how early humans evolved and lived.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Biology" (जीव विज्ञान): The general study of living organisms; too broad, not specifically about the evolution of mankind.

• Option 2: "Anthology" (संकलन): A collection of literary works such as poems or short stories by different authors; unrelated in meaning, despite sounding similar to "Anthropology".

• Option 4: "Psychology" (मनोविज्ञान): The study of the human mind and behaviour, not of human evolution.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions often confused in SSC due to similar spelling: "Anthropology" (study of mankind) vs "Anthology" (collection of writings) vs "Etymology" (study of word origins) vs "Entomology" (study of insects).

• Other "study of" one-word substitutes: Archaeology (study of ancient artefacts/history), Ornithology (study of birds), Zoology (study of animals).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

This book (1)_________ writing practice to pre-schoolers to help them learn to write (2)_________ of the English alphabet. Directional arrows, (3)_________ with the letters and numbers, guide children in writing. (4)_________ and copying activities encourage children to read and write letters and numbers (5)_________ to count.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. provides.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "This book", which is singular (third person singular).

• Rule — Simple Present Tense, Subject-Verb Agreement: With a singular third-person subject (he/she/it or a singular noun), the main verb in the Simple Present Tense takes an "-s/-es" ending.

• Since the sentence is a general, factual statement about what the book does (its purpose/function), the Simple Present Tense is required, giving "This book provides..."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "provide" is incorrect because it is the base form used with plural subjects or "I/you/we/they", not with the singular subject "This book".

• Option 3: "is providing" is incorrect because the Present Continuous Tense suggests a temporary, ongoing action, whereas the sentence describes the book's general, permanent function.

• Option 4: "had provided" is incorrect because the Past Perfect Tense is used for an action completed before another past action; there is no such past context here.

NOTE

• In descriptions of what a book/device/system generally does, the Simple Present Tense is the default and most natural tense in English.

• Remember to add -s/-es to the verb whenever the subject is a singular noun or he/she/it in the Simple Present Tense.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

This book (1)_________ writing practice to pre-schoolers to help them learn to write (2)_________ of the English alphabet. Directional arrows, (3)_________ with the letters and numbers, guide children in writing. (4)_________ and copying activities encourage children to read and write letters and numbers (5)_________ to count.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. letters.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "...help them learn to write letters of the English alphabet." The English alphabet is made up of individual letters (A, B, C, etc.), and since more than one letter is being referred to, the plural form "letters" is grammatically correct.

• The rest of the passage also refers to "letters and numbers" (plural) throughout, confirming that the plural form is consistent with the passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "letter" (singular) is incorrect because the sentence refers to the letters of the alphabet as a whole, which requires the plural form, and it is also inconsistent with the plural "letters and numbers" used later in the passage.

• Option 3: "phrases" is incorrect because a phrase is a group of words, not a component of the alphabet; pre-schoolers first learn to write individual letters, not phrases.

• Option 4: "words" is incorrect because the sentence specifically says "of the English alphabet", and the alphabet consists of letters, not whole words.

NOTE

• The alphabet is composed of letters; letters combine to form words; words combine to form phrases and sentences — a hierarchy worth remembering for such cloze questions.

• Always check the rest of the passage for consistency — the phrase "letters and numbers" reappears later, confirming the plural "letters" here.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

This book (1)_________ writing practice to pre-schoolers to help them learn to write (2)_________ of the English alphabet. Directional arrows, (3)_________ with the letters and numbers, guide children in writing. (4)_________ and copying activities encourage children to read and write letters and numbers (5)_________ to count.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. given.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Directional arrows, given with the letters and numbers, guide children in writing."

• Rule — Reduced (non-finite) relative clause: The phrase "given with the letters and numbers" is a reduced form of the relative clause "which are given with the letters and numbers". When the relative clause is in the passive voice, it is reduced using the past participle (V3) form of the verb.

• Since "arrows" are given/provided (a passive sense — the arrows do not give themselves), the past participle "given" correctly modifies "Directional arrows".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "giving" is incorrect because it would imply the arrows themselves are actively "giving" something, which does not match the intended passive sense.

• Option 3: "give" is incorrect because the base form cannot function as a participle modifying "arrows" in this construction.

• Option 4: "gave" is incorrect because the simple past tense form cannot be used as a participial modifier in a reduced relative clause.

NOTE

• Reduced relative clauses use the -ing form (V1+ing) for active meaning (e.g., "the man driving the car" = "who is driving") and the past participle (V3) for passive meaning (e.g., "the letter written by him" = "which was written").

• This is a commonly tested cloze/error-spotting concept in SSC exams — always check whether the noun being modified performs the action (use -ing) or receives the action (use V3).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

This book (1)_________ writing practice to pre-schoolers to help them learn to write (2)_________ of the English alphabet. Directional arrows, (3)_________ with the letters and numbers, guide children in writing. (4)_________ and copying activities encourage children to read and write letters and numbers (5)_________ to count.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Tracing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Tracing and copying activities encourage children to read and write letters and numbers..."

• Rule — Gerund as subject: When a verb form is used as the subject of a sentence, it must be in the gerund (-ing) form, and when two such activities are joined by "and", both must be in the same parallel form.

• The sentence already contains "copying" (a gerund) joined by "and" to the blank; for grammatical parallelism, the blank must also be a gerund, giving "Tracing and copying activities" — a compound subject.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Traced" is incorrect because a past participle cannot function as a parallel subject noun alongside the gerund "copying".

• Option 2: "Being traced" is incorrect because this passive gerund form is unnecessarily wordy and does not match the simple active gerund "copying" for parallel structure.

• Option 4: "Trace" is incorrect because the base form of the verb cannot function as a noun/subject here; it breaks parallelism with "copying".

NOTE

• Rule of Parallelism: When two or more items are joined by a conjunction like "and", "or", "but", they must all be in the same grammatical form (all gerunds, all infinitives, all nouns, etc.).
◦ Example: "Reading, writing and tracing are important skills" (all gerunds) — NOT "Reading, writing and to trace...".

• This parallelism rule is frequently tested in SSC error-spotting and cloze passage questions.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

This book (1)_________ writing practice to pre-schoolers to help them learn to write (2)_________ of the English alphabet. Directional arrows, (3)_________ with the letters and numbers, guide children in writing. (4)_________ and copying activities encourage children to read and write letters and numbers (5)_________ to count.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. as well as.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "...encourage children to read and write letters and numbers as well as to count."

• Rule — "As well as" (addition connector): The phrase "as well as" is used to add an extra element to a list, meaning "in addition to" or "and also". It correctly links the additional skill "to count" to the previously mentioned skills of reading and writing letters and numbers.

• The overall sense of the sentence is additive (listing multiple skills the activities help develop), not contrastive, which rules out connectors of contrast.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "but" is incorrect because it is a contrastive conjunction, used to show opposition between two ideas, which does not fit the additive sense required here.

• Option 3: "for" is incorrect because it is typically used to mean "because" (a reason connector), which does not fit the sentence's meaning of adding another skill.

• Option 4: "yet" is incorrect because, like "but", it is a contrastive conjunction (meaning "nevertheless"), which does not match the additive listing of skills in the sentence.

NOTE

• Connectors of addition: as well as, in addition to, along with, besides, moreover.

• Connectors of contrast: but, yet, however, although, whereas — these are commonly tested against additive connectors in SSC cloze and fill-in-the-blank questions.
